Worse part of trusting to authority for our privacy:

Those authorities aren’t even smart.
Or maybe they’re not dumb at all, they just don’t care, and they’re literally selling us.

This is a story about Flock, a surveillance company in the United States.

> Flock sold the idea of its services to the U.S. government, installed its cameras all over the country, and later claimed that crime rates had decreased in the cities where they placed their cameras.

These aren’t just traffic cameras for reading license plates , Flock’s Condor cameras are pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras, designed to record and track people, using both automatic and manual tracking for facial recognition.

These cameras were set up in various cities across the U.S.

Three different angles ~>

> First, are crime rates actually decreasing as they claimed? 

The answer is a Big No,
It’s really easy to do some research and check which countries have lower crime rates and whether they are implementing millions of cameras.
No, they don’t. They just provide a better quality of life for their citizens.

Cities like London, China, and some in the U.S. have the highest number of cameras monitoring their citizens. You can check and compare their crime rates. 

> Second, do only police departments have access to these videos, as they claim?

Hell no. Literally everything is exposed on the web, and you can check it yourself.

https://t.co/3d2SXuiezd

> Third, FLOCKY Folks Foked us

is Flock really a tech company, or just a camera factory?

They claim to offer AI-powered cameras for reading plates in high-security settings and bulletproof privacy cases. But if you live in the U.S. and a Flock camera is nearby, you should know that right now someone in the Philippines is watching you and actually getting paid for it. Creepy and dangerous.

Media 404 is exposing this.

Everything , including cars, models, the color of your clothes, even your skin, plate numbers, movements, etc. 
gets tagged from a basement in the Philippines. They have access to do this on behalf of Flock, for machine learning (ML).

So what’s up? What happens next?
Even police or government access is not justified when unauthorized, and it doesn’t really help reduce crime. But this? This is beyond ridiculous.

And what if a terrorist decides to literally use this system and target those gig workers?

Flock goes for gig workers because they’re cheap, with zero tax and no insurance. So, what stops terrorists from tracking this data, using cheap labor to gain access, and even tracking law enforcement officers? 
Could they decide to set up another 9/11?

> Then WHO IS responsible?

Privacy is not negotiable.
It’s a fundamental right.

Some greedy companies, authorities, centralized systems, and fancy bankers aren’t doing anything except making their houses bigger.

> Rules are good; they keep order. 
But some rules are broken by those who write them, and some rules only serve an elite group , with a contract behind it, waiting to be signed. 
Not every rule is good. Slavery was once a rule, a law, but it wasn’t good.

> And that’s what is happening today against all of us: 
MODERN SLAVERY that doesn’t care about skin color, but where PRIVACY is a PRIVILEGE , and some people have the right not to sell ourselves, but our data and everything we do.
